Distributed Volunteer Grid

Volunteer Compute Cockpit

Help explore unknown mathematical packings and break Erich Friedman benchmark bounds. Donate processing power directly in your browser or run the high-performance standalone binary. Both options submit verified solutions to the same shared coordinator grid.

Option 1: Standalone Worker (Fastest)
Multi-Threaded

Pure Rust Standalone Binary

Native multi-threaded Rayon engine (4+ CPU cores) with background daemon capability. Executes at peak hardware throughput with zero browser overhead.

# CLI operations & daemon config:
./shape-packing-worker
./shape-packing-worker edit # open config in text editor
./shape-packing-worker reconfigure # reset config & rerun wizard
./shape-packing-worker autostart enable
Download Releases → Windows (.exe), Linux, macOS
Option 2: In-Browser Web Cruncher (Zero Install)
Zero Install

Browser WebAssembly Engine

Zero install Wasm engine running in dedicated background web workers. Solve packing problems in real time with continuous visual oscilloscope feedback in this tab.

# In-browser execution features:
Wasm SIMD-accelerated geometric shrinkage engine.
Configurable Web Worker thread pools for parallel crunching.
Real-time state streaming to architectural oscilloscope canvas.
